title: Design System: DH & AI in African Studies

display.purpose: Hero only, once per site. Instrument Serif at its largest fluid step.

page-title.purpose: The PageHeader h1 on every route.

card-title.purpose: Paper titles, participant names, session names. Fluid so the step down from Section survives on wide screens.

lede.purpose: Standfirst under a page title. Outfit Light, muted ink, capped at 46ch.

prose.purpose: Body copy and abstracts. 400 weight, capped at 68ch.

eyebrow.purpose: Small tracked uppercase label above a heading, in brass ink.

meta.purpose: Field labels, session times, card metadata. Tracked uppercase in muted ink.

badge.purpose: The EN/FR language chip and session-type labels.

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Card hover, paired with a -2px lift.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions; also the global default.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The default action. Pressed teal with white text; lifts 1px and deepens on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.5rem; font-family: var(--font-sans, 'Outfit', system-ui, sans-serif); font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1; border: 0; border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; cursor: pointer; white-space: nowrap; transition: background-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), border-color 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), box-shadow 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-btn-primary { background-color: #0b6163; color: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(4 40 40 / 0.05); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background-color: #094e50; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px -2px rgb(4 40 40 / 0.08), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(4 40 40 / 0.04); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0d7377; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Accent Button
components.description: The one gold moment per page. Solid brass with ink text — never white, which fails contrast on a light tone.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn ds-btn-accent">Download the call for papers</button>

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outline variant: 1.5px teal border, deep-teal label, 10% teal wash on hover.

components.name: Ghost Icon Button

components.name: Filter Input
components.description: Search field on listing pages. Icon inset left; border warms to teal on hover; global focus ring.

components.description: The shared pick-one idiom on listing pages. Inner radius subtracts the tray's 0.25rem padding so the curves stay concentric.

narrative.overview:
This is the visual language of an institute of advanced study: a quiet, warm room where the scholarship is the thing on display and the furniture knows it. The page is warm paper rather than screen-white, the display face is a serif that behaves like set type, and the interface withdraws until it is needed. Nothing here competes with an abstract, a paper title, or a participant's name.

The restraint is structural, not timid. Hierarchy is carried almost entirely by typography — fluid serif sizes with tightening negative tracking as they grow — so the layout needs very few boxes, rules, or shadows to stay legible. Colour follows the same logic: deep teal does the institutional work of links, actions, and focus, while brass appears solidly exactly once per page and otherwise survives as a hairline, a two-pixel rule, or a six-percent wash. A grain texture sits at 3.5% over dark surfaces to keep large fields of colour from reading as flat digital ink.

The system takes paper seriously in a literal sense too: there is a real print stylesheet, prose is capped by character measure rather than container width, numerals are tabular, and the call for papers is expected to be printed and circulated. Two constraints shape every decision — the site is fully bilingual with English and French as equals, and it must stay light enough for a participant on mobile data in Stellenbosch.
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream page (#fdfbf7); screen-white is reserved for raised surfaces, so elevation reads as a lightness step
Serif display at a single weight (400); hierarchy from fluid size and negative tracking, never from bold
Brass used solidly once per page; everywhere else it is a hairline, rule, or wash
Shadows tinted warm with teal-black (rgb 4 40 40), never neutral
Semantic role tokens that flip once for dark mode instead of ~40 scattered dark: variants
Motion is short, eased, and fully surrendered under prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The One Gold Moment Rule
rules.body: Brass appears as a solid fill exactly once on any given page — the .btn-accent. Everywhere else it is a 2px rule, a hairline border, or a 6% wash. Its rarity is what makes it read as gold rather than as yellow.

rules.name: The Gold-Is-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: --accent (#c49528) is a graphics colour. Any brass text uses --accent-ink (#7a5c15). Setting body or label text in secondary-500 or secondary-600 fails WCAG AA on cream and is a defect, not a style choice.

rules.name: The Cream-Never-White Rule
rules.body: The page is #fdfbf7. Pure white is reserved for raised surfaces. A screen-white page background breaks the elevation model, because lifted is expressed as a step toward white.

rules.name: The Serif-Structures Rule
rules.body: Every heading level is Instrument Serif at 400. Hierarchy comes from fluid size and progressively tighter negative tracking — never from weight, and never from Outfit. A bold serif heading is off-system.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Reading text is capped by characters, not by container. Prose is 68ch, ledes 46ch. A container narrowed to fix line length is treating the symptom; the measure token is the fix.

rules.name: The Uppercase-Is-A-Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with wide tracking (0.16–0.18em) means this is a label. It is never a heading, never a sentence, and never body copy.

rules.name: The Four Containers Rule
rules.body: Pick one of the four containers: page 80rem, wide 72rem, readable 56rem, prose 44rem. A bespoke max-width on a page wrapper is a system violation — if none of the four fits, the missing one is a token, not a one-off.

rules.name: The Anchor Clearance Rule
rules.body: Anything that changes header height changes --nav-height, never a hard-coded offset. Three consumers depend on it staying the single source.

rules.name: The Rest-Is-Quiet Rule
rules.body: Surfaces sit at xs/sm at rest. The jump to lg plus a 2px lift belongs to hover alone. A card that is already lifted at rest has nowhere to go.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted rgb(4 40 40). A neutral or pure-black shadow is off-system and reads cold against cream.

rules.name: The Radius-By-Size Rule
rules.body: Bigger surface, bigger radius. Pills for badges and icon buttons, 1rem for cards, 0.75rem for buttons and inputs. A pill-shaped card or a sharp-cornered badge is off-system.

dos: Do reach for a semantic role (bg-page, text-body, border-subtle) rather than a palette step. The roles flip once for dark mode; a raw ramp value needs a hand-written dark: variant and will drift.
Do set brass text in --accent-ink (#7a5c15) and brass graphics in --accent (#c49528).
Do keep every heading in Instrument Serif at 400 and let size and tracking build the hierarchy.
Do cap reading text with --measure-prose (68ch) or --measure-lede (46ch).
Do give any new interactive control a 2.75rem minimum touch target and confirm it against the existing --control-h baseline.
Do put motion behind the tokens (--duration-base, --ease-standard) and confirm it disappears under prefers-reduced-motion.
Do check both locales and both themes before calling a change done. French runs roughly 20% longer, and several colours are defined only in the .dark block.
Do budget page weight deliberately. A meaningful share of participants arrive on mobile data.
donts: Don't use pure white as a page background, or neutral-black shadows. Both break the warm-paper model.
Don't add a second solid brass element to a page. One gold moment.
Don't introduce a bespoke max-width; use one of the four containers.
Don't bold a serif heading or set a heading in Outfit.
Don't hard-code a header offset; consume --nav-height.

Don't drift toward conference-brand energy — gradient heroes, urgency countdowns, Register now CTAs, sponsor tiers, stock photography of people at laptops. This is a scholarly record, not a commercial event site.
Don't drift toward tech-startup minimalism — screen-white, electric blue, sans-only, oversized pills, everything centred. The cream-and-serif world exists in deliberate rejection of it.
Don't drift toward institutional heaviness — crests, navy-and-maroon, justified dense serif, grey formal chrome. It would read as stuffy against an argument about equitable, forward-looking practice.

Don't ever reach for decorative Africanist or orientalist visual shorthand — ochre-and-sunset palettes, mudcloth or kente pattern fills, silhouette maps of the continent, ethnic display faces, acacia-and-savannah imagery. This is an explicit, user-confirmed prohibition. The workshop argues against extractive and stereotyping representation; the design must not enact what the scholarship critiques. Regional specificity, when it is wanted, comes from real content — people, places, institutions, and their own words — never from ornament.
